package_info.package_versions: N/A (potentially all versions at time of compromise)
package_info.why_malicious: The official PHP Git server was compromised in an attempt to plant a backdoor in the PHP source code, which would have affected all downstream users and websites relying on PHP. The intent was to introduce unauthorized code into the core PHP distribution, enabling remote code execution or other malicious actions on any server running the compromised PHP version.

execution_context.file_location: php-src/main/some_core_file.c (exact file not specified in report)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks if the HTTP User-Agent header contains the string 'zerodium'; if so, it executes arbitrary PHP code via zend_eval_string, enabling remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code introduces a hidden backdoor that allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary PHP code on any server running the compromised PHP binary, triggered by a specific User-Agent value.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal PHP source code should not contain hidden triggers or code execution paths based on HTTP headers. This is a clear violation of secure coding practices and supply chain trust.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Debugging or test builds might include conditional code, but never in production or public releases, and never with hidden triggers.
key_indicators: Conditional execution based on obscure HTTP header value
Use of zend_eval_string to execute arbitrary code
No legitimate reason for such a trigger in core PHP

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains unauthorized access to the official PHP Git server and injects a malicious commit containing a backdoor.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is merged into the PHP source code repository.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is distributed to users and organizations who download or build PHP from the compromised repository.
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromised PHP binaries are deployed on production servers.

attack_chain.action: At runtime, if an HTTP request with a User-Agent containing 'zerodium' is received, the backdoor executes arbitrary PHP code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote code execution on affected servers.

behavioral_signatures: Conditional code execution in core PHP files based on HTTP headers
Use of zend_eval_string or similar functions in unexpected locations
Hidden triggers (e.g., specific User-Agent values) enabling code execution
file_indicators: Unexpected changes or commits in core PHP source files
Presence of code referencing 'zerodium' or similar trigger strings
network_indicators: Unusual HTTP requests with User-Agent: zerodium
Outbound connections initiated by PHP processes in response to crafted requests (if backdoor enables callbacks)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized or suspicious commits in core PHP repositories, scan for conditional code execution paths based on HTTP headers, and audit for use of zend_eval_string or similar functions. Deploy runtime monitoring to detect unexpected code execution triggered by specific HTTP headers, and alert on HTTP requests with suspicious User-Agent values such as 'zerodium'.
